items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I went to Catholic school. I called him Cameroon and called his son John LeVoy.

ctx.x: Mm-hm. We put this march up to call Longfellow, 432. Longfellow's march was a real player of the pure. We went to the Shire, you know, everything started playing. La, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da, da. Joy looks, you know what to make there. But no doodle-doodle-doo there, you see. You play what you see there already. The fella said, well, what's the more I see tomorrow? I said, maybe about what? Oh, maybe that man can't really say, I don't think about…
Since that time. About what time was that?

By the way, about your schooling, how did you get your schooling? Did you go to a Catholic school or a private school? I went to Magdine 24th, private school. I went to 7 school. Did you go to the Catholic schools at all? I went to Catholic school. I called him Cameroon and called his son John LeVoy.
